# Model player weapon fire output in the balance harness

discovered-from:AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T (found while running the measured gate AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL).

## Problem statement

The Q3 = B measured gate for the weapon nerf (**Weapon upgrades are too powerful** (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T)) **cannot see a weapon-output change**. The closed-loop headless arena fires the player's shots on a fixed cadence constant:

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` → `FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS = 9`, `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED = 420`, `PLAYER_BULLET_LIFETIME = 0.75` — one bullet every 9 ticks regardless of the equipped weapon;
- the only import from `src/utils/weapons` in the whole `src/ai/eval/` tree is `import type { WeaponId }` — a **type-only** import, erased at compile time, so `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS`, `AOE_RADII`, hit budgets and `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` can never reach the simulation.

Measured, not inferred: the post-change 100-game campaign batch is **byte-identical** to the pre-change baseline (every per-run `recordsHash` included), and a sensitivity probe that temporarily raised `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS.cannon` from 2 to 12 (six times the starting weapon's cadence) also produced a byte-identical 3-game report. Evidence: `docs/BALANCING.md` §"Weapon 40 % trim / flattened curve — measured before/after gate".

## Why it matters

- Every future weapon damage/output tuning item that relies on the batch gate gets a guaranteed zero delta and a misleading "no effect" reading.
- The intended-experience bands (`src/data/experience-targets.json`) can never detect a weapon-output regression, because the metric input does not depend on weapon data.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` §Fidelity boundary already documents the limitation ("the arena's auto-fire is fixed"); this item closes it deliberately rather than leaving it implicit.
- The weapon-trim epic's own acceptance evidence (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T / AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL) rests on the numeric strength budget because the batch gate is blind — so the harness capability gap is a live, load-bearing limitation, not a cosmetic one.

## Users

*As the balancing agent, I want the headless arena to fire with the equipped weapons and their level-resolved statistics, so a weapon damage, cadence or pattern change moves the batch metrics and the measured gate can actually answer the question it was created for.*

Supporting user stories:

- *As a balance agent running `npm run evaluate -- --batch`, I want a weapon-value change to move `survivalSeconds` / `enemiesDestroyed` / `waveReached`, so I can accept or reject a weapon tuning change from the batch report.*
- *As a producer reviewing a weapon change, I want the documented `docs/BALANCING.md` fidelity boundary to state that weapon output is modelled, so I am not told "the gate cannot see this" again.*
- *As a future maintainer, I want the arena to consume the one shared weapon catalogue and level resolver, so a firearm change in the game and the harness cannot drift apart.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The arena's player projectiles are spawned from the resolved equipped weapon(s) (pattern count, offsets, cadence, lifetime) rather than a fixed `FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS` bullet, asserting that a level-resolved weapon change changes the arena's damage output.
- [ ] A sensitivity test proves the harness now **sees** a weapon-output change: the same-seed batch differs when a weapon's cadence, pattern count or AOE radius changes (the inverse of the AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL probe).
- [ ] Weapon levels resolved from the run's ownership context feed the arena's fire output, so a `weapon-level` choice is observable in the metrics.
- [ ] No duplicated weapon constant or resolver exists in `src/ai/eval/`; the arena consumes `src/utils/weapons.ts` / `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`.
- [ ] `src/data/experience-targets.json` is re-baselined (`targetsVersion` bumped) and GDD §2.7 updated in the same change.
- [ ] `docs/BALANCING.md` §Fidelity boundary and the weapon-trim evidence section are updated to state that weapon output **is** modelled.
- [ ] The full project test suite passes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **Parity rule (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1).** Shared game behaviour lives once in `src/scenes/core/` and shared dispatchers; no arena-local copy of a weapon constant or resolver may exist. The arena must consume `src/utils/weapons.ts` and `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`.
- **Scope guard.** Do not retune any weapon value in this item. This is an instrument-capability change only; if the newly-sensitive gate reveals an out-of-band weapon experience, that is follow-up work.
- **Determinism.** The arena must stay seed-deterministic: the same seed + policy + build produces identical records on the same commit (the existing `arena.test.ts` contract). New weapon scheduling must draw from the existing seeded stream only.
- **No CI/CD pipeline tests.** Not applicable to this item.
- **Fidelity boundary is honest, not aspirational.** Whatever is *not* modelled after this change must remain explicitly listed in `docs/BALANCING.md` §Fidelity boundary (e.g. homing arcs, chain lightning jumps, cluster split trajectories, timed field-pickup weapons if left out).
- **Re-baseline in the same change.** The metrics move by design, so `experience-targets.json` (`targetsVersion` bump) and GDD §2.7 must be updated together with the arena change, or the experience validation will fail on `dev`.

## Existing state

Measured from the tree on `dev` (commit `63801fa0`):

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` (1485 lines) has a single `fireCooldown` counter and a fixed auto-fire block: `fireCooldown = FIRE_INTERVAL_TICKS` (9 ticks), one `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED = 420` bullet down the facing vector, `PLAYER_BULLET_LIFETIME = 0.75`. `PLAYER_BULLET_*` constants are arena-local.
- The only weapon-module reference is `import type { WeaponId } from '../../utils/weapons'` (line 170) — type-only, erased at compile time.
- `HeadlessChoicePlayer` (`arena.ts` ~line 748) already records permanent weapon grants in `_weaponLevels` (`equipWeapon(id, permanent=true)` increments level starting at 1) and exposes `getWeaponLevels()` → `ChoiceContext.weaponLevels`. **Those recorded levels are never used for firing** — the arena's `world.playerBullets` path ignores them entirely.
- The game's `Player` (~`src/entities/Player.ts`) is the authority: `_permanentWeapons` always contains `'cannon'`; `getActiveWeapons()` returns permanent weapons + live timed weapons; `getWeaponLevel(id)` = permanent grants + temporary stacks (base 0); `resolveWeaponAtLevel(id, level)` / `resolveWeaponDefinition` / `resolveWeaponPattern` live in `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`; the catalogue, `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS`, `AOE_RADII`, hit budgets and `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS` live in `src/utils/weapons.ts` / `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`.
- The arena already models hostile force-field hits (`fieldHits`) and decrements `hostile.health -= 1` per bullet hit; there is **no per-weapon damage, pierce budget, bounce or AOE** in the arena today.
- `src/data/experience-targets.json` is at `targetsVersion: 1` with bands `{survivalSeconds, mineralsCollected, upgradesSelected, waveReached, levelReached, avoidableHits}`.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` §Fidelity boundary (line ~973) says `auto-fire` is modelled but "the chosen weapon's fire pattern … [is] not simulated (the arena's auto-fire is fixed)". `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts` asserts that section and the weapon-trim evidence section exist, so both must be updated consistently.
- Existing tests: `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` asserts determinism, telemetry shape, and that `playerBullets` exist (`playerBullets.length > 0`), plus `HeadlessChoicePlayer` permanent-grant level recording. No test ties firing to a weapon.

## Desired change

The arena's player fire output becomes a function of the resolved equipped weapons and their levels, consuming the shared catalogue/resolvers:

1. Resolve the run's owned weapon levels from the same ownership context the hold-full choice flow maintains (`ChoiceContext.weaponLevels`, plus the always-active `cannon` at level 0), mirroring `Player.getActiveWeapons()` / `getWeaponLevel()`.
2. For each active weapon, derive cadence from `resolveWeaponAtLevel(id, level).fireRateMs` (quantised beat grid), and spawn the weapon's resolved shot: `projectileCount`, `spreadAngle` / offsets, `bulletSize`, `bulletLifetime`, and `aoeRadius` (for AOE weapons), using `resolveWeaponPattern` / `expandWeaponPattern` where a pattern is needed.
3. Keep the shared seams: no new weapon constants in `src/ai/eval/`. Any scheduling/pattern helper that would be useful to the game belongs in the shared core, not duplicated in the arena.
4. Re-baseline `src/data/experience-targets.json` (`targetsVersion` bump) and update GDD §2.7 from a fresh post-change 100-game campaign batch, in the same change.
5. Update `docs/BALANCING.md` §Fidelity boundary and the weapon-trim evidence section to state weapon output **is** modelled; update `balancingDocs.test.ts` assertions accordingly.
6. Re-run the weapon-trim gate evidence (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T / AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL) afterwards, so the 40 % trim finally has a measured before/after.

## Suggested approach

1. Replace the fixed auto-fire with the shared weapon resolution: use `resolveWeaponAtLevel` / `resolveWeaponPattern` from `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` plus `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` / `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS` / `AOE_RADII` from `src/utils/weapons.ts`; spawn per-weapon projectiles (pattern count, offsets, lifetime, size, pierce budget, bounce, AOE radius) rather than one bullet down the facing vector.
2. Resolve the arena's weapon levels from the same ownership context the hold-full choice flow already maintains (`ChoiceContext.weaponLevels`), so a chosen `weapon-level` upgrade rung changes the arena's output exactly as it does in `Player`. The cannon is always active at level 0 (mirroring `Player._permanentWeapons = new Set(['cannon'])`).
3. Keep the change inside the shared code (gym↔game parity rule, AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): no arena-local copy of a weapon constant.
4. Re-record a baseline: the metrics will move by design, so `src/data/experience-targets.json` must be re-baselined (`targetsVersion` bump) with GDD §2.7 updated in the **same** change.
5. Re-run the weapon-trim gate evidence (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T / AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL) afterwards, so the 40 % trim finally has a measured before/after.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — the fixed auto-fire and projectile model; `HeadlessChoicePlayer` ownership context; the fire/spawn loop.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — the catalogue, cadence, pattern and level resolvers to consume (`resolveWeaponAtLevel`, `resolveWeaponDefinition`, `resolveWeaponPattern`, `expandWeaponPattern`, `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, `DEFAULT_WEAPON_SUBDIVISIONS`, `AOE_RADII`).
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — reference semantics for active weapons, levels and fire intervals.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — the arena behaviour and determinism tests; add the sensitivity tests here (or a dedicated sibling test file).
- `src/data/experience-targets.json`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.7 — the re-baseline and narrative.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — the fidelity boundary and the before/after evidence; `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts` asserts it.
- `src/ai/eval/metrics.ts`, `src/ai/eval/report.ts`, `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — only if a new observable (e.g. a damage/output counter) is added; prefer existing metrics.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: over-modelling.** A full per-weapon mechanics model (homing arcs, chain jumps, cluster split trajectories, ricochet bounce vectors) is large and can destabilise determinism. The acceptance bar is the sensitivity test (AC2) on cadence / pattern count / AOE radius; extra mechanics are modelled only as far as needed and anything left out stays documented.
- **Risk: re-baseline churn.** Re-baselining `experience-targets.json` and GDD §2.7 in the same change can move the documented intended-experience bands substantially (the arena becomes genuinely weapon-sensitive). Mitigated by deriving the bands from a fresh 100-game campaign batch and recording before/after in the work item.
- **Risk: parity drift.** A new arena-local scheduling/pattern copy would violate AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1. Mitigated by the repo-wide duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs assertion.
- **Risk: determinism break.** A new fire schedule that draws on `Math.random()` or wall-clock time would break the seed-deterministic batch. Mitigated by drawing only from the existing seeded stream and keeping the existing `arena.test.ts` determinism assertions green.
- **Scope-creep risk.** If the newly-sensitive gate reveals that the shipped weapon values are out of band, that is a *balance* finding, not this instrument item. Record it as a linked follow-up work item; do not retune weapons here.

### Assumptions (recorded, not blocking)

- **A1 — "weapon output" definition.** The harness models the resolved firing parameters the game's `Player` uses: cadence (`resolveWeaponAtLevel(...).fireRateMs`), projectile count / spread / offsets, bullet size, lifetime, and AOE radius, plus (where cheap and shared) hit budget / bounce. Exotic per-weapon mechanics are modelled only as far as the sensitivity test needs.
- **A2 — active weapons.** The arena fires the permanent cannon at level 0 plus every permanent weapon grant recorded by the hold-full choice flow, mirroring `Player.getActiveWeapons()`. Timed field-pickup weapons remain out of scope (the arena's drop model stays generic); if included cheaply they must still resolve through the shared catalogue.
- **A3 — re-baseline is expected.** Unlike AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL (where no band moved), the metrics *will* move by design here, so the `targetsVersion` bump and GDD §2.7 update are expected, with the exact band centres/tolerances derived from the post-change batch.
- **A4 — instrumentation only.** No weapon value is retuned in this item.
- **A5 — determinism.** The batch remains reproducible on the same commit; the sensitivity tests compare same-seed batches and assert difference, while a control same-seed pair asserts equality.

## Related work

Precedent and context (curated):

- **Weapon upgrades are too powerful (AH-0MVRENEME004FS8T)** — the parent epic whose Q3 = B measured gate exposed this gap; its strength-budget evidence is the numeric half of the gate, and this item is the mechanism half.
- **Post-change measured gate and targets re-baseline (AH-0MVWAVM03002FLLL)** — recorded the byte-identical before/after batch and the sensitivity probe that proved the arena is blind to weapon output.
- **Capture pre-change weapon balance baseline (AH-0MVWAVJJG003S0XF)** — the baseline sweep shape (`--batch --games 100`, campaign, `competent`, `--ticks 18000`) that the post-change re-baseline should reuse.

## Problem

`scripts/evaluate.mjs --tune` edits a tracked balance CSV in place and journals the pre-edit bytes beside it (`src/data/<file>.tune-journal`). Both paths are process-global, not per-run:

1. **Startup reconcile steals a live journal.** `main()` reconciles `<csv>.tune-journal` before anything else (crash recovery). A journal is written before the edit and removed after the restore, so it exists for the whole candidate sweep of a *running* process — a second `--tune` run on the same CSV reconciles it, restoring the CSV underneath run 1.
2. **Two runs interleave edits.** Run 2 writes its own journal over run 1's, then restores from run 2's bytes while run 1 continues its candidate sweep against a file run 2 may have rewritten.

Discovered while fixing AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS: the `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` watchdog case asserted "no `*.tune-journal` anywhere in `src/data`", which failed when a sibling suite in the same parallel Vitest run held a journal at the same shared path. The suite was fixed for the shared path (the assertion is now scoped to the run's own pid), but the product-level hazard remains for real concurrent CLI invocations.

## Impact

Two designers (or a designer plus a scripted tuning sweep) tuning the same balance CSV at once can silently produce a comparison against the wrong CSV bytes, and the crash-recovery journal can be consumed by the wrong run. Single-run usage is unaffected.

## Suggested approach

Pick one, cheapest first:

- **Lock file**: an exclusive `<csv>.tune-lock` (O\_EXCL) held for the whole run, with a bounded wait and a clear exit-2 diagnostic naming the holder pid. The journal's pid is already recorded, so the holder is identifiable.
- **Refuse concurrent runs**: on `writeJournal`, if a journal exists whose pid is alive (`kill(pid, 0)`), abort with exit 2 naming that pid instead of overwriting it.
- **Per-run temp CSVs**: out of scope — `--tune` deliberately edits the tracked file so the candidate sweep reads it through the shared config store.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Two concurrent `--tune` runs on the same CSV cannot interleave: the second either waits (bounded) or exits non-zero with a diagnostic naming the holding pid.
2. A live journal is never reconciled by another process: crash recovery only consumes a journal whose pid is dead.
3. `scripts/evaluate-tune-progress.test.ts` and `scripts/csvEditJournal.test.ts` still pass, including the pid-scoped journal assertions added by AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS.
4. `docs/BALANCING.md` documents the concurrency rule alongside the crash-safe journal section.
5. Full suite passes (`/skill:test`).

## Related work

- discovered-from:AH-0MW251IE0006K5DS (the test-failure item that surfaced the shared-path race).

## Goal

Make the dev-only telemetry recorder cheap enough that it does not distort a measured run.

**User story:** As a developer profiling the game, I want the dev telemetry recorder to stay out of the frame budget, so a profile measures the game and not the recorder.

## Evidence (measured, AH-0MVXV0E8000937U5)

CPU profile of \`PlayScene\` level 10 demo (60 s, desktop headless Chromium), with the dev recorder enabled:

- \`sanitiseObject\` (\`src/telemetry/redact.ts:93\`) 0.18 % of the measured window, \`sanitise\` (\`src/telemetry/redact.ts:65\`) 0.15 %, \`utf8ByteLength\` (\`src/telemetry/devUpload.ts:180\`) 0.14 %, \`write\` (\`src/telemetry/sinks.ts:50\`) 0.08 %, \`deepFreeze\` (\`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:459\`) 0.16 % — **~0.7 % of the window / ~7 % of JS**.
- The same run logged a skipped run-end upload: 15.8 MiB of run telemetry exceeded the 8 MiB browser→node message cap, so the recorder was serialising a payload it then discarded.

## Scope

- Avoid serialising/redacting a payload that will be discarded for exceeding the upload cap (check the size first, or stream/bound the recording).
- Keep redaction guarantees intact: no unredacted payload may ever reach a sink.

## Out of scope

- Production telemetry behaviour (the recorder is dev-only).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A run whose telemetry exceeds the upload cap no longer pays the full serialise+redact cost before discarding (verified by a test on the size-guard seam).
2. Redaction tests still pass (no path skips redaction for a payload that is written).
3. In the same profiled demo run, the telemetry bucket share is measurably lower, with the before/after numbers recorded on this item.
4. Full project test suite passes.

## Problem statement

After AH-0MW2IRYAH0055WCN, the per-frame `Graphics` draw-submission surface was removed, but the **software-rasteriser** `GymPerformance` run at `--cpu-throttle 4` still measures **24.3–24.6 FPS** against the ≥ 30 FPS mobile-tier bar. No further main-thread JS work can close it.

**Crucial update since this item was filed:** the *hardware*-WebGL mobile tier has since been measured and **clears the ≥ 30 FPS bar with room** — AH-0MW3KP1R90030QY9 (completed) records four `GymPerformance` runs at 4× throttle with `--gpu --require-hardware-webgl`: **59.44 FPS** in-band (load 9.25), and **53.77 / 50.57 / 46.85 FPS** out-of-band (load 16.43 / 17.29 / 23.20), p50 at the 16.7 ms vsync step. `native` falls 76.92 % → 16.35 %. **Headline:** A performance-testing skill that sweeps enemy counts in 50-enemy steps with semi-random, representative loadouts to determine the playable enemy count ceiling with reproducible FPS data.

## Problem / goal

The repo can measure one fixed load (`GymPerformance`, exactly 100 enemies with
live fire — AH-0MVXV0DT50028RF8) but there is no repeatable way to answer "how
many enemies can we actually hold at a playable frame rate?". The producer has
to pick the load by hand, run the harness several times, and reconcile the
numbers themselves.

As the producer, I want **a performance testing skill** that automatically
walks the enemy load upward in 50-enemy steps until the game stops being
playable, so I get a headroom curve (min / max / average FPS per load) from one
command instead of a series of ad-hoc runs.

## Expected behaviour

Invoking the skill (e.g. `/skill:perf-sweep`, final name to be decided at plan
time) runs a **sweep**:

1. **Load steps of 50 enemies**, starting at 50 (`50, 100, 150, …`).
2. At every step the measured load is **enemies that both shoot and dive** —
   live fire and diving behaviour on screen, not idle targets. The **mix of
   shooting and diving archetypes varies per step**, chosen from a fixed seeded
   roster (the existing stress gym already includes `diver` and `raider`), and
   the mix is recorded with the step.
3. At every step the **player has a semi-random, representative loadout**
   (defined concretely under *Resolved design decisions*): weapons drawn from
   **each broad weapon category**, **at least one power-up**, filled up to the
   shipped six-slot cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`). Weapon and power-up
   **levels are not maxed**: they are set to a level *representative of the
   campaign level a hex of the configured aggression deploys at*. The chosen
   loadout and its levels are recorded with the step.
4. The **player fires** (auto-fire on) with the full loadout — the measured
   frame cost includes the player's own bullets and kills.
5. Each step is measured for **at least 15 seconds** (warm-up excluded from the
   measurement window, and reported).
6. Per step record **min, max and average FPS** (plus p50/p95 frame time, long
   frames, and live enemy/bullet counts — the harness already produces these).
7. **Iterate until a step's average FPS is below 30**, then stop: that step is
   the reported failure point and the previous step is the last playable load.
   A hard ceiling (e.g. 400 enemies) and a total-run budget guard against a
   runaway sweep.
8. **Report the results to the user** at the end: a summary table of every step
   (enemy count, loadout + levels, shoot/dive mix, min/average/max FPS,
   verdict) plus the headline ("playable to N enemies; first failure at M with
   average X FPS") and the path to the machine-readable JSON report.

## Resolved design decisions (producer answers)

These replace the five open questions from the seed description. Answers are
the producer's, with the concrete, testable interpretation the implementation
must pin.

1. **Skill location — project-local.** The skill lives in the repo at
   `.pi/skills/<skill-name>/` and may reference the repo's harness. Editing
   `.pi/` is normally restricted; this item is the explicit instruction to add
   this skill. *Producer answer: "project-local".*

2. **"Full loadout" — semi-random and representative.** The loadout is built
   through the shipped seams (`Player.equipWeapon(id, permanent)` per level and
   `Player.collectPowerUp(id, permanent)`), never a test-only fork, and fills
   at most the six-slot cap (`POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP`).
   - **Broad categories** to draw from (one weapon from each, subject to the
     six-slot cap): *conventional projectile* (`spread`, `dual`, `rapid`),
     *beam/hitscan* (`wave_laser`), *area-of-effect* (`nova`, `mortar`, `arc`),
     and *exotic/positional* (`ricochet`, `cluster`, `options`, `rear_guard`,
     `broadside`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug`). The permanent
     `cannon` is always present as the base weapon.
   - **At least one power-up** from `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`.
   - **Remaining slots** are filled with a seeded random choice of the
     remaining weapons/power-ups, still respecting the six-slot cap.
   - **Levels are not maxed.** Weapon collection level and power-up level are
     derived from the campaign level a hex of the configured `--aggression`
     deploys at (`deploymentLevelForAggression(aggression)` →
     `hexAggressionLevel`, campaign level 1–`MAX_LEVEL` = 1–10): a
     representative upgrade index scaled from the fraction of the campaign
     climbed, clamped **below** each weapon's upgrade cap, so a late aggression
     is strong-but-not-maxed. The exact scaling constant is a plan-time tuning
     constant; the rule and every derived level are recorded per step.
   - *Producer answer: "Semi-Random, include weapons from each broad category and
     at least one power-up. Don't max the levels — make them somewhat
     representative of the level they would be if attacking a hex of the
     defined aggression."*

3. **Shoot-and-dive mix — vary it.** Each step's enemy roster mixes shooting
   and diving archetypes, with the **proportion varying per step** (seeded, and
   recorded), rather than one fixed ratio throughout the sweep. The roster is
   fixed at step setup so the load is constant for that step. *Producer answer:
   "vary them".*

4. **The player shoots — yes.** Auto-fire is enabled with the step's loadout,
   so the measured load includes player bullets and kills. Enemies are **not**
   made invulnerable: the step spawns its target N at step start and the live
   enemy/bullet counts are recorded through the window (N is the peak/target
   load). *Producer answer: "Yes".*

5. **Step comparability — fixed seed + fixed duration.** The sweep runs an
   **as-played, deterministic mode**: one seed for the whole run and a fixed
   per-step duration mean the same seed reproduces the same loadout sequence and
   (with the scene's own seeding) the same evolution. Kill-free/invulnerable
   enemies are explicitly *not* used. The report records the seed, the fixed
   duration and the "as-played" mode. *Producer answer: "fix seed + duration".*

## Design outline (to be confirmed at plan time)

- Reuse the existing harness rather than writing a second one:
  `scripts/measure-performance.mjs` (`perfProbe`, `--seconds`, `--warmup`,
  `--cpu-throttle`, `--scene`, `--out`) and its pure maths in
  `scripts/perf-report.mjs`.
- The scene must accept an **enemy count parameter**, a **semi-random loadout
  setup** and a **per-step shoot/dive mix**. Options to choose between at plan
  time: (a) parameterise `GymPerformance`/`GymFormationScene` (it already takes
  `config.count` and `buildOffsets(count)`) rather than adding a scene; or
  (b) add a sweep gym. Preference is (a) — one scene, one code path, no
  divergence — with the parity matrix updated only if a new scene is genuinely
  required.
- The loadout must be applied through the shipped/shared path (no test-only
  re-implementation of weapon or upgrade behaviour), so the measured frame cost
  is the frame cost a player would pay: `Player.equipWeapon(id, true)` L times
  for a weapon level L, and `Player.collectPowerUp(id, true)` for a power-up
  level, respecting the six-slot cap.
- The sweep orchestration should be a small, unit-testable pure planner (step
  list, stop rule, summary) driven by a thin CLI/script, so the stop rule and
  summary are tested without booting a browser.
- Loadout selection and the shoot/dive mix must be **seeded and recorded**, so
  a run can be reproduced (`seed` in the report; same seed → same loadout
  sequence and same mixes).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A performance-testing skill exists, is discoverable by name, and its
   documentation states the sweep, the load definition, the 15 s minimum
   measurement window and the stop rule.
2. One command runs the whole sweep unattended on the reference host: enemies
   in 50-enemy increments, each step with enemies that shoot **and** dive (mix
   varying per step), the player firing a **semi-random** loadout that draws a
   weapon from each broad category and **at least one power-up** up to the
   six-slot cap, with **non-maxed levels representative of the configured
   aggression's campaign level**.
3. Every step measures for **at least 15 seconds** (warm-up excluded) and
   records **min, max and average FPS**, alongside the frame-time percentiles,
   long-frame counts and live enemy/bullet counts.
4. The sweep stops at the **first step whose average FPS is below 30**, records
   that step as the failure point, and reports the previous step as the last
   playable load; a documented ceiling/timeout prevents a runaway sweep.
5. The final report is printed to the user as a per-step table plus a headline
   verdict, and the same data is written to a machine-readable JSON report that
   names the scene, step list, loadout **and levels** per step, shoot/dive mix,
   seed, host and commit.
6. The loadout and shoot/dive mix are seeded and recorded; re-running with the
   same seed produces the same loadout sequence and same mixes (unit-tested).
7. The step planner, stop rule and summary are covered by fast unit tests (no
   browser); the scene's parameterised enemy count, loadout and mix seams are
   covered by scene tests; the full suite is green via the test skill and
   typecheck is clean.
8. Gym↔game parity is preserved: the measured scenario runs shared core code,
   any new/changed gym is registered in the capture registry and
   `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, and no simulation loop is forked.
9. Usage is documented (skill docs plus a link from the performance docs /
   README harness section) and one recorded sweep on the reference host is
   published with the provenance the `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` "Recorded:" rule
   requires (commit, date, host, backend, throttle).

## Out of scope

- Optimising anything found by the sweep (a regression or hotspot becomes its
  own child/discovered-from item, per parent AC6).
- Changing the existing budget (60 FPS desktop / >= 30 FPS mobile) or the
  existing `GymPerformance` 100-enemy rows.
- Mobile/CPU-throttled sweeps (the skill may accept `--cpu-throttle` as a
  pass-through, but no throttled sweep is recorded by this item).
- Electron-host sweeps beyond what the existing harness already supports.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPerformance.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`
  — parameterise the enemy count, the player loadout and the shoot/dive mix
  (`config.count`, `buildOffsets(count)`, `createEnemyFromConfig`,
  `fireForEnemy`).
- `src/core/perfProbe.ts` — the probe and `PerformanceCounts` seam the sweep
  samples (no change expected).
- `scripts/measure-performance.mjs`, `scripts/perf-launch.mjs`,
  `scripts/perf-report.mjs` — the harness the sweep drives.
- `scripts/perf-sweep.mjs` *(new, likely)* — step planner + sweep driver.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `equipWeapon(id, true)` / `collectPowerUp(id,
  true)` the loadout grant uses.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP` (six-slot cap the loadout
  respects).
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarDeployment.ts`,
  `src/core/hangarWar/hexDifficulty.ts` — `deploymentLevelForAggression` /
  `hexAggressionLevel` (campaign level the loadout levels derive from).
- `src/core/rules.ts` (`POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`), `src/powerups/types.ts`,
  `src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — weapon/power-up
  catalogue and level maths.
- `.pi/skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md` *(new)* — the skill itself (project-local).
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md`, `README.md` — usage + the recorded sweep.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`,
  `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts` — only if a gym changes/arrives.

## Notes / constraints

- Measurement policy: agent-initiated test runs go through the test skill; the
  sweep itself is a measurement tool, not a test run, and must not be wired
  into the vitest suite (same rule the existing harness follows).
- Noise floor: compare only within one host load band, and record the host,
  backend and load per step (parent AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87 AC6, and the
  `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` noise-floor rule).
- The host can be busy with other agents' suites; the sweep should record each
  step's host load so a noisy sweep is identifiable rather than silently
  published.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep:** The skill may be expected to evolve into a full benchmarking
  or regression-comparison tool. Mitigated by explicit out-of-scope items and
  recording hotspots as separate discovered-from items.
- **Non-determinism from randomness:** Seeded loadouts and mixes reduce but do
  not eliminate concerns about reproducibility across hardware. The seed +
  recorded per-step loadout/levels/mix provide traceability.
- **Sweep duration at high counts:** 400 enemies × 15 s = 600 s minimum; add a
  total-run budget (e.g. 30 min) and enforce a step ceiling.
- **Player-fire decay:** Because the player fires and enemies are not
  invulnerable (producer decision 4), the live enemy count decays within a
  step; N is the peak/target load and the live counts are recorded. If a decayed
  load proves to under-measure sustained load, that becomes a discovered-from
  item, not scope creep.
- **Level derivation:** "Representative of the aggression's campaign level" is
  a documented scaling rule, not a second difficulty system; it reuses
  `hexAggressionLevel`, and the exact scaling constant is tuned at plan time.
- **Gym↔game parity risk:** Adding parameters to `GymFormationScene` must not
  cause a divergence that isn't captured in `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`. The parity
  capture tests will flag this.

## Related work

- `discovered-from:AH-0MW3KP1R90030QY9` — filed while re-measuring the mobile
  tier on hardware WebGL; the sweep is the natural next step after the fixed
  100-enemy rows.
- Related: **Optimization pass** (AH-0MVWJQUN6009IS87) and its performance
  children — **Frame-time performance harness for `PlayScene` (headless
  p50/p95/FPS)** (AH-0MVXV0DER009ER70), **`GymPerformance` stress gym — 100
  late-game enemies with live fire** (AH-0MVXV0DT50028RF8), **Publish
  performance budget, harness usage and results
  (docs/PERFORMANCE.md)** (AH-0MVXV0FUP006W8OR), **Re-measure the mobile tier
  on hardware WebGL and close parent AC5 (4x CPU throttle, quiet host)**
  (AH-0MW3KP1R90030QY9).
- Related: **Increase the possible number of enemies in a enemy formation to
  200** (AH-0MTV8Q1LV001KOA5) — the formation cap bounds how large a sweep step
  can be; confirm it before claiming a 200+ step is reachable.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Recorded from the interactive intake interview (producer replies, this session).

- **Q1 — Where does the skill live?** Project-local `.pi/skills/` or a global
  skill? — **Answer (producer):** "project-local". Source: interactive reply,
  2026-11-06.
- **Q2 — What is a "full loadout"?** Which weapons/upgrades, random subset of a
  maxed set or fixed maxed slots, whether power-up levels are maxed —
  **Answer (producer):** "Semi-Random, include weapons from each broad category
  and at least one power-up. Don't max the levels — make them somewhat
  representative of the level they would be if attacking a hex of the defined
  aggression." Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-06. Research: the shipped
  seams are `Player.equipWeapon(id, true)` / `Player.collectPowerUp(id, true)`,
  the six-slot cap is `POWER_UP_SLOT_CAP = 6`, and `deploymentLevelForAggression`
  → `hexAggressionLevel` maps aggression to campaign level 1–10.
- **Q3 — What is the shoot-and-dive archetype mix?** Which archetypes shoot vs
  dive, and in what proportion — **Answer (producer):** "vary them". Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-06. Interpretation: the proportion varies per step,
  seeded and recorded; the fixable roster includes the stress gym's `diver` and
  `raider`.
- **Q4 — Does the player shoot?** — **Answer (producer):** "Yes". Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-06. Interpretation: auto-fire on; enemies are not
  made invulnerable; live counts recorded.
- **Q5 — How do we keep steps comparable?** — **Answer (producer):** "fix seed +
  duration". Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-06. Interpretation: as-played
  deterministic mode; one seed + fixed per-step duration; kill-free enemies not

# Less bright minerals colour

## Headline

Reduce the brightness of the mineral collectable colour so that when many
minerals appear on screen simultaneously the field is less visually
overwhelming, while retaining clear gold/yellow identity.

## Problem statement

The current mineral body colour (`0xffdd44`, a very bright gold) is too
intense when multiple minerals are present on the screen, reducing visual
clarity and contributing to screen clutter.

## Users

- **Player**: Needs to distinguish minerals from other on-screen elements
  (enemy bullets, explosions, power-ups) when many minerals are scattered
  across the play area.
- **Gym users**: Same concern applies in the minerals gym (`GymMinerals`)
  where mineral density can be high.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The mineral body colour is changed from `0xffdd44` to a more subdued yellow
  (proposed: `0xccaa33` — approximately 20% reduction in brightness while
  preserving the golden hue).
- Ordinary minerals remain visually distinct from salvage minerals (orange
  `0xff7a2e`) and deposit minerals (red `0xff1744`).
- Minerals remain visually distinct from enemy bullets (red `0xff4444`,
  orange `0xffaa00`, deep-orange `0xff6600`) and the thrust flame
  (`0xff8c00`).
- The change applies consistently to both the shipped game (`PlayScene`)
  and all gyms that display minerals (e.g. `GymMinerals`), since both
  consume the same `MINERAL_COLOR` constant.
- Full project test suite passes with the change.

## Constraints

- The colour must remain recognisably gold/yellow to preserve the mineral
  identity.
- Salvage and deposit mineral colours must remain distinct and unchanged.
- No other gameplay behaviour changes.

## Existing state

- `MINERAL_COLOR` is defined in `src/core/constants.ts` as `0xffdd44`.
- The `Mineral` entity class uses this constant as the default fill colour
  for the rendered dot (via `_drawBody()`).
- Both the game and all gyms import the same constant; there is no
  gym-specific override.

## Desired change

Update `MINERAL_COLOR` in `src/core/constants.ts` to a more subdued value.
No other code changes are required as the constant is consumed directly
by the `Mineral` class.

# Make Phase Shift single-use like Teleport (one activation, readiness timer)

## Problem statement

The two automatic defensive consumables now use **different** use/regeneration
models, and the asymmetry is visible in play, the HUD, the level catalogue and
the tuning gym:

- **Teleport** is **single-use** (AH-0MVY096RT006QMF4): the player holds exactly
  one warp, spending it starts **one** level-derived recharge timer (60 s base
  → 20 s cap), and a pickup or hold-full grant **readies** it. There is no
  stored count and no FIFO.
- **Phase Shift** is a **charge pool**: up to 3 charges, each spent charge
  starts its own recharge timer (30 s base → 10 s cap), a field pickup grants a
  level-derived number of charges, and the `phaseCharges` level axis raises the
  cap from 1 to 3.

So the same class of automatic life-saving defence costs one activation for
Teleport but can bank up to three for Phase Shift. The dedicated recharge-tuning
gym (AH-0MV82IAYG000WS8B) had to document the mismatch, and the HUD/catalogue
copy differ for two abilities the player experiences side by side.

The producer wants **Phase Shift to behave the same as Teleport with respect to
uses and regeneration**.

## Users

- **As a player**, spending Phase Shift should cost the same as spending
  Teleport: one activation, then a single level-derived recharge wait before it
  is available again — not a three-charge reserve.
- **As a balance designer**, both automatic defensive abilities should share one
  use/regeneration model so recharge tuning, HUD presentation and reward
  surfaces stay consistent.

## Current behaviour (evidence)

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `PowerUpLevelStore` treats Phase Shift as a
  pooled consumable: `_charges`, `_rechargeTimers`, `consumePhaseCharge()`,
  `phaseCharges()`, `_poolCap()` / `consumableChargeCap()` (the `phaseCharges`
  axis: 1 → 3). Teleport instead uses the single `_teleportRecharge` readiness
  timer (`consumeTeleport`, `hasTeleport`, `isTeleportRecharging`,
  `teleportRechargeRemaining`).
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — the auto-defence feed treats Phase Shift as
  "charges > 0" and Teleport as "ready"; the 50/50 tie-break
  (AH-0MW231NAR008K9IS) compares those two states.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — the Phase Shift row shows a `×N` charge count; the Teleport
  row shows readiness plus a `next in Ns` countdown (AH-0MW231O8Q0095LQM).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `phaseCharges` is a levelled axis
  (base 1, cap 3); Teleport deliberately has **no** warp-count axis
  (AH-0MVY096RT006QMF4).

## Desired behaviour

Phase Shift adopts Teleport's **single-use readiness** model:

1. The player holds **exactly one** Phase Shift activation.
2. Spending it (automatic defence) starts **one** recharge timer whose duration
   is the level-derived Phase Shift recharge time at the moment of consumption
   (`phaseRechargeRate` 30 s base → 10 s cap).
3. When the timer elapses Phase Shift is ready again.
4. A Phase Shift **field pickup** or **hold-full grant** readies it (timer 0)
   instead of banking a charge; a pickup landing mid-recharge readies it
   immediately (mirrors the Teleport pickup rule, AH-0MW231MTT005DE90).
5. No stored count, no FIFO, no multi-charge pool: the readiness timer is the
   whole Phase Shift state (mirrors `_teleportRecharge`).
6. Auto-defence selects Phase Shift only when **ready** and Teleport only when
   **ready**, with the existing uniform 50/50 tie-break when both are ready; a
   recharging Phase Shift drops out of the draw.
7. The HUD Phase Shift row matches the Teleport single-use presentation
   (readiness state + `next in Ns`), with no `×N` count.
8. The recharge-tuning gym (AH-0MV82IAYG000WS8B) continues to work: its Phase
   Shift slider tunes the single readiness recharge time.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Single-use store.** `PowerUpLevelStore` holds at most one Phase
  Shift activation; spending it starts exactly one recharge timer at the
  level-derived `phaseRechargeTime`, and a completed timer readies it. Exposed
  readiness API mirrors Teleport (`hasPhaseShift`/`isPhaseShiftRecharging`/
  `phaseShiftRechargeRemaining` or equivalent).
- [ ] **AC2 — Grants ready, never bank.** A Phase Shift field pickup and a
  hold-full reward both set Phase Shift ready (timer 0); a grant mid-recharge
  readies it immediately. No grant can create a second stored activation.
- [ ] **AC3 — Auto-defence readiness.** The shared auto-defence resolver spends
  Phase Shift only while ready; when both Phase Shift and Teleport are ready the
  existing uniform 50/50 tie-break applies; a recharging Phase Shift is never
  selected.
- [ ] **AC4 — HUD parity.** The HUD Phase Shift row uses the single-use
  presentation (readiness + `next in Ns`) with no `×N` charge count and no
  multi-charge grey-out copy; covered by HUD tests.
- [ ] **AC5 — Level catalogue.** The `phaseCharges` axis is retired (or
  documented as inert with no consumer); `phaseRechargeRate` (30 s → 10 s)
  remains the single level-derived interval, matching Teleport's no-count axis.
  Catalogue/resolver completeness and monotonicity tests updated.
- [ ] **AC6 — Checkpoint round-trip.** A checkpoint preserves Phase Shift's
  readiness/recharge remaining time exactly as it does Teleport's readiness
  clock; a legacy checkpoint carrying a Phase Shift charge count loads without
  error (coerced to a valid single-use state).
- [ ] **AC7 — Gym ↔ game parity.** `PlayScene`, every gym and
  `GymRechargeTuning` consume the one shared model (no divergent copies); the
  `CombatScene.equivalence` duplicate-body guard and parity suites pass.
- [ ] **AC8 — Documentation.** GDD §4.4 / §4.4.3, README and code comments
  describe Phase Shift as single-use (readiness + countdown), including the
  reload/level-derived recharge rule. `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (managed by
  the ship release pipeline).
- [ ] **AC9 — Verification.** `npm run typecheck` and the full project test
  suite pass with no build warnings.

## Constraints

- **Teleport is the reference; do not change it.** Its single-use behaviour,
  recharge interval and pickup-readies rule stay as shipped.
- **Supersedes** the Phase Shift **pooled** parts of AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR (and
  the cap-3 Phase Shift expectations in AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT/
  AH-0MV82I7HF009ZHPD). Keep the shared recharge-timer engine
  (`tickRecharge`) and the level-derived `phaseRechargeRate` — only the
  use/regeneration *shape* changes.
- **Backward compatible:** existing saved/checkpoint blobs must load; an old
  Phase Shift charge count is coerced to a valid single-use state rather than
  throwing.
- **No magic numbers:** reuse the catalogue axis and the shared seams/messages.
- Do not touch `.pi/`, `skill/`, `command/` or agent-infrastructure directories.

## Related work

- AH-0MVY096RT006QMF4 — *Teleport regenerates too quickly* (established the
  single-use Teleport model this item copies).
- AH-0MW231LVW008P2QE / AH-0MW231MCL000MMUU / AH-0MW231MTT005DE90 /
  AH-0MW231NAR008K9IS / AH-0MW231O8Q0095LQM / AH-0MW231NRP004HAT5 /
  AH-0MW231OPF007WSTF — the single-use Teleport spec, store readiness, pickup
  readies, 50/50 tie-break, HUD row, reward retirement and docs sweep.
- AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR — *Teleport and Phase Shift should recharge* (original
  recharge model; Phase Shift pooled parts superseded by this item).
- AH-0MV82I7TX0009JMT / AH-0MV82I7HF009ZHPD — per-charge recharge engine and
  cap-3 (engine retained; Phase Shift multi-charge retired).
- AH-0MV82IAYG000WS8B — **discovered-from**: the recharge-tuning gym exposed the
  asymmetry and currently documents it; its sliders must keep working.
- AH-0MVY3IGRC00954UD — checkpoint persistence of consumable pools/readiness.
- AH-0MVTQMREN009DSFW — consumable upgrades should not be endless.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — Phase Shift single-use readiness path
  (mirroring `_teleportRecharge`), remove pooled consumption.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — catalogue `singleUse` flag for `phase_shift`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — readiness accessors + auto-defence feed.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — single-use Phase Shift row and countdown.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`,
  `src/ui/HUD.test.ts`, checkpoint tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`, and code comments.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymRechargeTuning.ts` — comments/docs only; behaviour should

## Duplicate check

Searched the worklog for `Phase Shift`, `single-use`, `recharge`, `charge pool`,
`readiness model`, `Phase Shift one use`, `single-use Phase Shift`,

children) and the original recharge model (AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR), which this item
partially supersedes for Phase Shift.

## Impact

Spending Phase Shift will feel like spending Teleport — one activation, one

and the HUD, catalogue and tuning copy stop contradicting each other.
